tldr: The paper studies the dynamics of a social compass model for opinion depolarization using the Ott-Antonsen Ansatz.
motivation: Previous work focused on steady states; this work aims to understand the dynamics leading to depolarization.
method: The authors apply the Ott-Antonsen Ansatz to reduce the macroscopic dynamics to a finite-dimensional ODE system and perform linear stability analysis.
result: The critical coupling for depolarization depends only on the first inverse moment of the conviction distribution, while the depolarization rate depends on higher moments.
conclusion: Conviction distributions with the same critical coupling can exhibit vastly different depolarization timescales, and the analysis extends to community structure.

title: A Unified Framework For Sensitivity Comparison Across Stimulated Raman, Stimulated Raman Photothermal, And Mid-infrared Photothermal Microscopy
authors: Takuro Ideguchi Keiichiro Toda
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Label-free vibrational microscopy based on Raman scattering and mid-infrared (MIR) absorption has advanced biological imaging through the development of diverse high-sensitivity modalities. However, rigorous sensitivity comparisons across these techniques remain lacking. Here, we establish a unified theoretical framework for quantitatively comparing the shot-noise-limited sensitivities of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS), MIR photothermal (MIP), and stimulated Raman photothermal (SRP) microscopy. The framework is built on two quantities: an effective absorption coefficient, which places SRS on the same footing as linear absorption, and a photothermal (PT) factor, which isolates the contribution specific to PT readout. Using experimentally realistic parameters, we show that MIR absorption coefficients for representative polar vibrational modes are typically about two orders of magnitude larger than the effective absorption coefficients of SRS, even for strong off-resonant Raman bands. In MIP, however, this intrinsic advantage is partly offset by a small PT factor, limiting the net sensitivity gain over SRS to several-fold and, at most, about one order of magnitude. In SRP, by contrast, burst-pulse thermal accumulation substantially increases the PT factor. Under ideal shot-noise-limited conditions with matched per-pulse excitation-energy conditions in water, SRP is predicted to provide sensitivities several-fold higher than those of SRS and to approach those of MIP. This framework provides a common basis for sensitivity assessment across vibrational imaging modalities and clarifies how absorption strength, photothermal accumulation, and readout conditions determine the practical advantages of each modality.
tldr: A unified theoretical framework for comparing shot-noise-limited sensitivities of stimulated Raman, mid-infrared photothermal, and stimulated Raman photothermal microscopy.
motivation: Lack of rigorous sensitivity comparisons across label-free vibrational microscopy techniques hinders optimal modality selection for biological imaging.
method: Develops a framework using effective absorption coefficient and photothermal factor to quantitatively compare SRS, MIP, and SRP under shot-noise-limited conditions.
result: MIR absorption coefficients are ~100x larger than SRS effective absorption, but MIP's sensitivity gain is limited to several-fold due to small PT factor; SRP with burst-pulse thermal accumulation approaches MIP sensitivity.
conclusion: The framework provides a common basis for sensitivity assessment and clarifies how absorption strength, photothermal accumulation, and readout conditions determine practical advantages.

title: pyDOF: A Python Library For The Design Of Discrete Forward And Inverse Filters
authors: Z. Nikolaou, P. Domingo, L. Vervisch, D. Drikakis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present pyDOF, a Python-based software library which provides a domain-specific framework for the design of symmetric, physical-space, forward as well as inverse discrete filters. pyDOF is based on a constrained optimisation framework developed in our previous work [1, 2]. This framework allows the user to impose a wide range of constraints on the discrete filter transfer-function such as monotonicity, positivity, value-fixing, gradient-smoothing etc. amongst many others. pyDOF additionally includes an adaptive filter stencil selection option, and a van Cittert-based inverse-filter design with a user-controlled reconstruction order. The filter coefficients are computed automatically, and saved to a plain text file which can be readily parsed by any programming language. pyDOF can be used to design a wide range of low-pass, high-pass, multi band-pass/band-stop etc. discrete filters. In addition, due to its generality and abstraction, pyDOF can be used to design specific filters for user-defined target filter transfer functions. Although developed primarily for application to computational fluid dynamics simulations, pyDOF can be used to design discrete filters for a wide range of signal processing applications.
tldr: pyDOF is a Python library for designing discrete forward and inverse filters, primarily for computational fluid dynamics.
motivation: To provide a flexible, constraint-based framework for designing custom discrete filters for signal processing and CFD applications.
method: The library implements a constrained optimization framework to compute filter coefficients with user-specified constraints, including adaptive stencil selection and van Cittert-based inverse filtering.
result: pyDOF can generate a wide range of low-pass, high-pass, and multi-band filters, outputting coefficients to a text file for easy integration.
conclusion: The library is a practical tool for filter design in CFD and other signal processing domains, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Human Adaptive Variability Stabilises Collective Traffic Dynamics
authors: Shirui Zhou, Ching Jin, Junfang Tian, Shiteng Zheng, Rui Jiang, Shiquan Zhong, Shoufeng Ma, Vittorio Loreto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated systems are often designed on the assumption that replacing human behavioural variability with precise, uniform algorithmic control improves collective performance. In automotive traffic, this principle underlies commercial adaptive cruise control (ACC). Using two large-scale human-driving experiments comprising 2.95 million car-following observations, a 25-vehicle platoon experiment and a controlled 11-driver protocol, cross-validated with 0.77 million observations from the NGSIM dataset and data from 22 production ACC systems, together with empirically calibrated ACC simulations, we show the opposite: rigid algorithmic uniformity creates systemic fragility. Commercial rule-based controllers amplify small local perturbations into severe stop-and-go waves, increasing fuel consumption and carbon emissions by approximately 2.7- to 5.0-fold across scenarios. Human-driven platoons, by contrast, progressively dissipate disturbances and maintain smoother flow. We identify the behavioural mechanism behind this advantage: human car-following does not follow a fixed proportional spacing rule. Drivers continuously reshape their time-headway distributions across speed regimes, exhibiting a non-monotonic shift from efficiency-oriented to risk-sensitive regulation. This speed-dependent variability generates nonlinear damping that suppresses the synchronisation and propagation of local errors. Our findings challenge the view that human variability is merely suboptimal noise to be eliminated. More broadly, they suggest that robust large-scale interactive AI systems should embed adaptive, human-inspired behavioural flexibility rather than rely on rigid uniformity.
tldr: This paper studies human driving variability in traffic flow, showing it stabilizes collective dynamics better than rigid algorithmic control.
motivation: To challenge the assumption that replacing human behavioral variability with precise algorithmic control improves collective performance, using traffic as a case study.
method: Two large-scale human-driving experiments (2.95M car-following observations, 25-vehicle platoon, 11-driver protocol) cross-validated with NGSIM dataset and 22 production ACC systems, plus empirically calibrated ACC simulations.
result: Rigid algorithmic uniformity creates systemic fragility, amplifying perturbations into stop-and-go waves with 2.7-5.0x higher fuel consumption and emissions, while human-driven platoons dissipate disturbances and maintain smoother flow.
conclusion: Human adaptive variability provides nonlinear damping that stabilizes traffic, suggesting robust AI systems should embed adaptive, human-inspired flexibility rather than rigid uniformity.

title: Bounds Of Triangular Subnorms And Their Algorithms
authors: Xue-Ping Wang Ting Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article deals with the upper and lower bounds of triangular subnorms generated by continuous, strictly decreasing additive generators. It first establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for the comparability of such triangular subnorms. It then explores the existence of strict (resp. nilpotent) bounds of a finite family of strict (resp. nilpotent) triangular subnorms generated by continuous, strictly decreasing additive generators. By duality, completely analogous results are derived for triangular superconorms generated by continuous, strictly increasing additive generators. In particular, it supplies the corresponding algorithms for computing those bounds, which are illustrated by several examples.
tldr: The paper studies bounds of triangular subnorms generated by continuous, strictly decreasing additive generators, with algorithms for computing these bounds.
motivation: Triangular norms and subnorms are used in fuzzy logic and aggregation theory; the paper aims to characterize their comparability and bounds.
method: The authors establish necessary and sufficient conditions for comparability of triangular subnorms, and derive algorithms for computing strict or nilpotent bounds of finite families.
result: Conditions for comparability are given, and algorithms for computing bounds are provided, illustrated with examples.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of triangular subnorms and their duals, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fa\`a Di Bruno Is Taylor Composition
authors: Heinrich Hartmann
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that reduced Taylor polynomials compose: for [MATH] maps [MATH] and [MATH] between Banach spaces, [MATH] where [MATH]. The proof is a direct estimate of the Peano remainder and requires no combinatorics or partition arguments. From this we derive the multivariate Fa\`a di Bruno formula in partition form (Levy 2006), by polarization, and in multi-index form (Constantine-Savits 1996) by coefficient extraction. As an application we give a higher-order product rule in three forms.
tldr: The paper proves that reduced Taylor polynomials compose and derives the multivariate Faà di Bruno formula from this composition property.
motivation: To provide a simple, combinatorial-free proof of the composition of Taylor polynomials and to unify different forms of the multivariate Faà di Bruno formula.
method: Direct estimation of the Peano remainder without combinatorics or partition arguments, followed by polarization and coefficient extraction.
result: Reduced Taylor polynomials compose, and the multivariate Faà di Bruno formula is derived in both partition form and multi-index form.
conclusion: The composition property of Taylor polynomials yields a clean derivation of higher-order chain rules and product rules.

title: Motive Theory Hidden In Karaji-Pascal Triangle
authors: Somayeh Habibi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These lecture notes are intended as an accessible introduction to some basic ideas of motive theory for readers with limited background in algebraic geometry. Mathematics often reveals unexpected connections between seemingly distant areas. A simple combinatorial identity may encode geometric structures, arithmetic information, or even sophisticated categorical phenomena. In these notes, we trace a path from elementary counting arguments to Voevodsky's theory of motives. We show how some classical combinatorial identities emerge naturally from geometry, and how motivic decompositions reveal the deeper geometric and arithmetic structures underlying them. Our guiding example is provided by the Karaji--Pascal identity and its [MATH]-analogue, which link combinatorics and algebraic geometry. Thus our primary aim of these lecture notes is to demonstrate that some familiar combinatorial identities can provide non-experts with an entry point to some of the basic ideas of motive theory! Moreover, while introducing the reader to the subject, we also hope to encourage the view that even an elementary mathematical formula may encode a deeper underlying geometric and arithmetic structure. Along the way, the notes offer a gentle introduction to motives through a concrete example rather than through the full technical machinery of modern theory.
tldr: Lecture notes introducing motive theory via combinatorial identities like the Karaji-Pascal triangle.
motivation: To provide an accessible entry point to motive theory for readers with limited algebraic geometry background.
method: Traces a path from elementary counting arguments to Voevodsky's motives, using the Karaji-Pascal identity as a guiding example.
result: Shows how classical combinatorial identities emerge from geometry and how motivic decompositions reveal deeper structures.
conclusion: Even elementary formulas can encode deep geometric and arithmetic structures, motivating further study of motives.

title: Lonely Solids
authors: Ivo Fagundes David de Oliveira, Tanya Khovanova, Yogev Shpilman
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A three-dimensional solid has the Rupert property if a congruent copy of the solid can pass through a hole cut through it without splitting it. We extend this idea to pairs of convex solids: two solids are called if each can pass through a suitable hole in the other. A solid is called if it has no friends, including itself. We show that a convex solid is lonely if and only if it has constant width. We also show that every convex solid that does not have constant width has a particularly simple friend: an arbitrarily long and arbitrarily thin rectangular cuboid. Finally, we prove that all non-constant-width convex solids lie in a single connected component of the friendship graph. More precisely, any two such solids are connected by a chain of at most ``three handshakes''.
tldr: This paper studies the Rupert property for convex solids, defining 'lonely solids' as those that cannot pass through a hole in any congruent copy of another convex solid, and proves that a convex solid is lonely iff it has constant width.
motivation: To extend the classical Rupert property (a solid can pass through a hole in a congruent copy of itself) to pairs of solids, and to characterize solids that have no such 'friends'.
method: Geometric and combinatorial arguments, including the concept of constant width and construction of rectangular cuboid friends for non-constant-width solids.
result: A convex solid is lonely iff it has constant width; every non-constant-width solid has a friend that is an arbitrarily long and thin rectangular cuboid; all non-constant-width solids are connected in a friendship graph by at most three handshakes.
conclusion: The notion of loneliness for convex solids is fully characterized by constant width, and the friendship graph of convex solids is highly connected.

title: Escher's Cubes: Tiling The Faces Of Polyhedra
authors: William Keehn Peter Kagey
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Isohedral or face-transitive polyhedra are polyhedra with identical faces, such that any face can be mapped onto any other via a symmetry of the polyhedron. Examples include the Platonic solids, Catalan solids, bipyramids, and trapezohedra. We use the orbit-counting theorem to count the number of ways of tiling the faces of such polyhedra up to their isometries given any arbitrary set of tile designs. This approach also counts tilings fixed under each isometry of a given polyhedron and provides explicit enumeration formulas. We use this framework to recover sixteen sequences from the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences and fill in the gaps by contributing twelve new sequences.
tldr: This paper uses the orbit-counting theorem to count tilings of isohedral polyhedra faces, contributing new sequences to OEIS.
motivation: To enumerate the number of ways to tile the faces of face-transitive polyhedra up to symmetry, filling gaps in known integer sequences.
method: Applies the orbit-counting theorem (Burnside's lemma) to count tilings under the symmetry group of each polyhedron, given any set of tile designs.
result: Recovers sixteen existing OEIS sequences and contributes twelve new sequences for various polyhedra.
conclusion: The combinatorial framework provides explicit formulas for tiling counts and can be extended to other symmetric structures.

title: Classifying The Groups Of Order $p^3$ In Lean
authors: Li Xiang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note discusses our formalisation in Lean 4 of the classification of groups of order [MATH] for a prime number [MATH], using mathlib4. We present the five isomorphism classes and give a detailed account of the formalisation, with particular emphasis on the non-abelian case, which requiring the most substantial formal development. For odd~[MATH], the non-abelian groups are the Heisenberg group [MATH] and the semidirect product [MATH]; for [MATH], they are [MATH] and [MATH]. We describe the construction of these concrete groups, the structural lemmas about centers, commutators, and exponents, and the explicit isomorphism constructions that classify an arbitrary non-abelian [MATH]-group.
tldr: This paper formalizes the classification of groups of order p^3 in the Lean 4 theorem prover.
motivation: To provide a verified formal proof of a classic group theory result, demonstrating the capabilities of the mathlib4 library.
method: The authors construct the five isomorphism classes explicitly, using structural lemmas about centers, commutators, and exponents, and provide explicit isomorphisms for non-abelian groups.
result: A complete formal classification of groups of order p^3 in Lean 4, covering both abelian and non-abelian cases.
conclusion: The formalization is successful and highlights the power of interactive theorem proving for algebraic classification problems.

title: Fuzzy Normed BCK-algebras And BCI-algebras
authors: Ravikumar Bandaru Young Bae Jun
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the notion of fuzzy normed BCK-algebras and fuzzy normed BCI-algebras as a natural extension of clas sical normed algebraic structures into the fuzzy setting. A fuzzy norm on a BCK/BCI-algebra is defined as a mapping from the algebra and a positive real parameter into the unit interval satisfying suitable axioms analogous to those of fuzzy normed linear spaces. Several examples are presented to illustrate the validity of the axioms. Fundamental properties of fuzzy normed BCK/BCI algebras are established, including monotonicity, chained triangle inequalities, and order-related behaviors. It is shown that every BCK/BCI-algebra admits a fuzzy norm, and the behavior of fuzzy norms under algebra homomorphisms is investigated. Necessary and sufficient conditions are obtained for the transfer of fuzzy norms via injective, surjective, and bijective homomorphisms. A charac terization theorem is proved showing that the main fuzzy norm inequality can be reduced to a simpler condition. These results generalize known concepts in fuzzy algebra and provide a new analytical framework for studying BCK/BCI algebras.
tldr: This paper introduces fuzzy norms on BCK/BCI-algebras, extending classical normed algebraic structures into the fuzzy setting.
motivation: To generalize normed algebraic structures to fuzzy logic and provide a new analytical framework for BCK/BCI-algebras.
method: Defines fuzzy norms axiomatically, provides examples, and studies properties like monotonicity and homomorphism transfer.
result: Every BCK/BCI-algebra admits a fuzzy norm, and conditions for transferring norms via homomorphisms are characterized.
conclusion: The work establishes a foundation for fuzzy normed BCK/BCI-algebras, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generating Functions And Analytic Properties Of Apostol-type Exponential B-splines
authors: Damla Gun
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spline functions, particularly B-splines, play a fundamental role in approximation theory, numerical analysis, and spectral representations. Although generating function techniques are widely used in combinatorics and special function theory, their systematic use in spline constructions remains relatively limited. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a generating function framework for the construction and analysis of generalized exponential B-spline families associated with Apostol-Bernoulli polynomials. Using backward shift operators and operator-based representations of uniform B-splines, we construct new Apostol-Bernoulli-type B-spline functions and derive explicit generating functions, recurrence relations, and structural identities. The present approach also yields generalized exponential spline families depending on the parameters [MATH], which interpolate between classical polynomial splines, exponential splines, and Apostol-type extensions. Furthermore, by combining de Boor recurrence relations with differential operator techniques, we establish analytic recurrence formulas involving parameter derivatives of the associated spline sequences. We also investigate the Fourier transform of the generating functions and obtain explicit rational-type representations in the frequency domain, revealing a direct connection between discrete difference operators, exponential spline structures, and spectral analytic behavior. These results provide a unified analytic approach for constructing generalized spline families and suggest further applications in approximation theory, operator-based spline analysis, and generalized spectral methods.
tldr: This paper introduces a generating function framework for constructing Apostol-type exponential B-splines, deriving recurrence relations and Fourier transforms.
motivation: To systematically apply generating function techniques to spline constructions, which have been underexplored in this context.
method: Uses backward shift operators and operator-based representations of uniform B-splines to construct new Apostol-Bernoulli-type B-spline functions, and combines de Boor recurrence with differential operators.
result: Obtains explicit generating functions, recurrence relations, structural identities, and rational-type Fourier representations linking discrete difference operators to exponential spline structures.
conclusion: Provides a unified analytic approach for generalized spline families with potential applications in approximation theory and spectral methods.

title: A Pedagogical Introduction To The Unified Transform Method: The Heat Equation On A Finite Interval
authors: Athanasios Paraskevopoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a detailed application of the Unified Transform Method (Fokas method) to the one-dimensional heat equation on [MATH] with Dirichlet boundary conditions. The analysis formulates the Initial-Boundary Value Problem and derives an integral representation of the solution via a generalised spatial Fourier transform with complex spectral parameter [MATH], yielding the Global Relation -- an algebraic identity coupling the initial datum, prescribed boundary values, and unknown Neumann data. The unknowns are eliminated by exploiting the symmetry [MATH], reducing the solution to a contour integral over [MATH]. An explicit evaluation is carried out for exponential initial datum [MATH] and Dirichlet conditions [MATH], [MATH]. The integral representation is analysed in the complex plane, with emphasis on exponential decay and analyticity, providing rigorous justification for contour deformation via Cauchy's Theorem and Jordan's Lemma. Numerical implementation in Maple uses a trapezoidal contour parametrisation ensuring exponential decay along each segment; the solution over [MATH], [MATH] matches prescribed data to machine precision. method: Formulates the problem using a generalized Fourier transform with complex spectral parameter, derives the Global Relation, and eliminates unknown boundary data via symmetry to obtain a contour integral representation.
result: Explicit evaluation for an exponential initial condition yields a solution that matches prescribed data to machine precision when implemented numerically in Maple.
conclusion: The Unified Transform Method is analytically and numerically effective for classical parabolic problems, with rigorous contour analysis ensuring stable and accurate solutions.

title: Lower Bounds On Mixing Rates For A Class Of Mixing Flows On Surfaces
authors: Miriam Lorenzo-Laguno
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study mixing rates for locally Hamiltonian flows on compact surfaces with asymmetric logarithmic singularities. For a full measure set of such flows, we show that the decay of correlations of smooth observables cannot be uniformly faster than a power of [MATH]. In particular, there exist sequences of times and observables for which correlations admit lower bounds of order [MATH] for any [MATH]. We further show that for a typical Arnol'd flow on [MATH], the self-correlation of every box in the minimal component is bounded below by [MATH] along an unbounded sequence of times. Motivated by questions in spectral theory, we also construct examples of such flows for which the self-correlation of a box fails to be square-integrable. These results complement previous upper bounds for correlations in both settings, which are also of polynomial order in [MATH], and show that logarithmic decay rates are essentially sharp along sequences of times.

motivation: To understand the sharpness of known polynomial upper bounds on mixing rates for certain Hamiltonian flows, and to address spectral theory questions.
method: The authors analyze locally Hamiltonian flows on compact surfaces with asymmetric logarithmic singularities, using techniques from dynamical systems and ergodic theory.

title: On The Optimal Prediction Of Extreme Events
authors: Stilian Stoev Benjamin Bobbia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The prediction of the extremely large values of a response variable [MATH] in terms of a vector of covariates [MATH] is a fundamental problem arising in many scientific and engineering domains. The scarcity of data in the extremes makes the optimal solution of this problem of particular importance. The optimal predictors of such events can be explicitly characterized in just a few cases and it is of fundamental practical and theoretical interest to develop optimal estimators over large classes of models and predictors. In this work, the focus is on the case where [MATH] have a multivariate regularly varying distribution and one seeks an optimal predictor expressed as a positive homogeneous function [MATH] of the covariates. The asymptotic prediction precision in this setting coincides with the tail-dependence coefficient [MATH] and it can be expressed as an integral functional of the associated angular measure of [MATH]. Thus, finding asymptotically optimal homogeneous predictors amounts to solving a variational problem. We obtain a general solution to this problem, which is expressed in terms of a non-extreme conditional quantile of a tilted distribution derived from the angular measure. This leads to a general inference methodology for the optimal predictors in the peaks-over-threshold framework form extreme value theory. We establish the universal consistency for these estimators over large classes of angular measures. A general-purpose implementation of the resulting inference procedure is shown to work remarkably well against optimal oracle estimators, as well as in the challenging problem of extreme solar flare prediction.
tldr: This paper develops optimal predictors for extreme events using multivariate regular variation and extreme value theory.
motivation: Predicting extremely large values of a response variable is crucial in many scientific domains, but optimal solutions are rare due to data scarcity in extremes.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a variational problem involving the tail-dependence coefficient and angular measure, and propose estimators based on non-extreme conditional quantiles of a tilted distribution.
result: They obtain a general solution for asymptotically optimal homogeneous predictors and prove universal consistency of their estimators over large classes of angular measures.
conclusion: The proposed inference methodology works well against optimal oracle estimators and is applied to extreme solar flare prediction.

title: Singular Morse-Smale Flows On Pseudomanifolds With Spherical-Cone Singularities: Conley Theory And Intersection Homology
authors: Jean-Paul Brasselet, Dahisy Lima, Denilson Ten\'orio
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical Morse-Conley theory provides powerful tools for relating dynamical and topological invariants of smooth manifolds. In this paper, we extend this perspective to pseudomanifolds with spherical-cone singularities. By introducing and investigating singular Morse-Smale flows on pseudomanifolds with isolated singularities whose links are homeomorphic to finite disjoint unions of spheres. We establish formulas for the Conley indices of spherical-cone singularities in terms of their local dynamics, prove the existence of global Lyapunov functions, and investigate the structure of the associated Lyapunov graphs. These results yield alternative formulas for the Euler-Poincar\'e characteristic expressed in terms of Conley-theoretic invariants. To relate the singular and smooth settings, we introduce a global morsification procedure that associates a smooth manifold [MATH] to a singular pseudomanifold [MATH]. This construction allows us to compare the topology of [MATH] and [MATH] and, in particular, to derive formulas relating their Euler-Poincar\'e characteristics. Finally, we study the intersection homology of pseudomanifolds with spherical-cone singularities. We establish connections between intersection homology, singular homology, and the Morse homology of the morsification, thereby providing a dynamical approach to the computation of intersection homology.
tldr: This paper extends Morse-Conley theory to pseudomanifolds with spherical-cone singularities, establishing Conley index formulas and connections to intersection homology.
motivation: To generalize classical dynamical systems and topological invariants from smooth manifolds to singular spaces, enabling analysis of flows on pseudomanifolds.
method: Introduces singular Morse-Smale flows on pseudomanifolds with isolated singularities whose links are spheres, defines Conley indices for singularities, and constructs a morsification procedure to relate singular and smooth settings.
result: Derives formulas for Conley indices of spherical-cone singularities, proves existence of global Lyapunov functions, and relates intersection homology to Morse homology of the morsification.
conclusion: Provides a dynamical approach to computing intersection homology and extends Conley theory to singular spaces, offering new topological invariants for pseudomanifolds.

title: Air Cargo Load And Route Planning In Pickup And Delivery Operations
authors: C. A. A. Sanches A. C. P. Mesquita
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the aerial pickup and delivery of goods in a distribution network, transport aviation faces risks of load imbalance due to the urgency required for loading, immediate take-off, and mission accomplishment. Transport planners deal with trip itineraries, prioritisation of items, building up pallets, and balanced loading, but there are no commercially available systems that can integrally assist in all these requirements. This enables other risks, such as improper delivery, excessive fuel burn, and possible safety issues due to cargo imbalance, as well as a longer than necessary turn-around time. This NP-hard problem, named "Air Cargo Load Planning with Routing, Pickup, and Delivery Problem" (ACLP+RPDP), is mathematically modelled using standardised pallets in fixed positions. We developed a strategy to solve this problem, considering historical transport data from some Brazilian hub networks, and performed several experiments with a commercial solver, five known meta-heuristics, and a new heuristic designed specifically for this problem. By using a portable computer, our strategy quickly found practical solutions to a wide range of real problems in much less than operationally acceptable time.
tldr: This paper addresses an NP-hard air cargo load and route planning problem with pickup and delivery, proposing a mathematical model and heuristic solution.
motivation: Transport aviation faces risks of load imbalance and inefficiency due to lack of integrated planning systems for cargo loading and routing.
method: The problem is modeled as an NP-hard optimization problem using standardized pallets in fixed positions, and solved with a commercial solver, meta-heuristics, and a custom heuristic.
result: The proposed strategy finds practical solutions quickly on real-world data from Brazilian hub networks, within operationally acceptable time.
conclusion: The approach effectively addresses the integrated load and route planning problem, reducing risks and improving turnaround time.

title: Preservation Of Primariness Under $\ell_1$-, $c_0$-, And $\ell_\infty$-sums Of Banach Spaces

title: The Devil In The (de)tails: An Improved Recovery Guarantee For Sparse Approximation
authors: Ben Adcock, Simone Brugiapaglia, Avi Gupta
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many functions exhibit approximate sparsity in their coefficients with respect to a given dictionary. In recent literature, sparse approximation in such a dictionary from i.i.d. pointwise samples, underpinned by compressed sensing, has become a powerful tool for high-dimensional function approximation. A key step in this framework is truncating the (typically countably-infinite) dictionary to a finite index set of size [MATH], so that compressed sensing tools can be used to approximate the function by a sparse combination of these truncated dictionary elements. This introduces a discrete [MATH]-truncation error over the sample points, which in standard approaches, is bounded by the continuous [MATH]-norm. Such a deterministic, worst-case bound ignores the randomness of the sample points entirely. As a result, [MATH] must be taken unnecessarily large to keep the truncation error under control, which directly inflates the size of the matrix involved in the sparse recovery algorithm and increases computational cost. In this paper, we show that by exploiting the i.i.d. structure of the sample points, the discrete [MATH] truncation error admits a bound that instead reflects the faster decay behaviour of the continuous [MATH]-norm truncation error and yields significantly smaller truncation sets and decreased computational cost. We demonstrate this through applications to weighted Wiener spaces and anisotropic Sobolev spaces, in each case obtaining significantly smaller truncation sets than recent works. In addition, we also present an improved bound of independent interest for sparse approximation in bounded Riesz systems, where the measurement condition exhibits a smaller (and scale-invariant) dependence on the Riesz constants than in previous works.
tldr: This paper improves recovery guarantees for sparse approximation from i.i.d. samples by exploiting randomness to reduce truncation set size.
motivation: Standard sparse approximation methods use a worst-case bound on truncation error, leading to unnecessarily large truncation sets and high computational cost.
method: The authors derive a probabilistic bound on the discrete ℓ2 truncation error that reflects the faster decay of the continuous ℓ2-norm truncation error, using the i.i.d. structure of sample points.
result: They obtain significantly smaller truncation sets for weighted Wiener and anisotropic Sobolev spaces, and an improved bound for sparse approximation in bounded Riesz systems with scale-invariant dependence on Riesz constants.
conclusion: Exploiting randomness in sampling yields more efficient sparse approximation with reduced computational cost.

title: Measured-Pattern-Aware Pinching-Antenna Systems With Coupling-Efficiency Optimization
authors: Hao Feng, Hui Yang, Ming Zeng, Yulei Wang, Ebrahim Bedeer, Nian Xia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pinching-antenna (PA) systems have been widely investigated as a flexible architecture for waveguide-enabled wireless transmission. Existing analytical models, however, often rely on isotropic radiation assumptions and simplified couplingefficiency settings, which may overlook two practical design factors: the geometry-dependent radiation pattern of each PA and the sequential extraction of guided power along the waveguide. In this paper, we propose a measured-radiation-pattern-aware PA framework that incorporates an externally obtained radiation pattern, waveguide attenuation, and coupling-dependent power extraction. For a single PA, the resulting placement rule balances directional gain, waveguide loss, and free-space path loss, leading to a coupling-efficiency threshold for outperforming a fixed isotropic antenna. For multiple PAs, we study phase-matched placement and coupling-efficiency design under both uniform and independently controllable coupling. The uniform-coupling case yields a one-dimensional optimality condition and reveals that the preferred coupling efficiency decreases as more phasematched PAs participate in coherent combining. The independently controllable case admits a closed-form power-allocation structure, where stronger effective directional channels receive larger radiated power fractions. Numerical results based on a representative measured PA radiation pattern demonstrate the importance of jointly accounting for measured-radiation-patternaware placement and coupling-efficiency optimization.
tldr: This paper proposes a measured-pattern-aware framework for pinching-antenna systems in wireless communications, focusing on coupling-efficiency optimization.
motivation: Existing pinching-antenna models assume isotropic radiation and simplified coupling, ignoring practical factors like geometry-dependent patterns and sequential power extraction.
method: The authors develop a framework incorporating measured radiation patterns, waveguide attenuation, and coupling-dependent power extraction, and analyze placement and coupling design for single and multiple PAs.
result: They derive placement rules and coupling-efficiency thresholds for single PAs, and for multiple PAs they find optimal coupling decreases with more phase-matched PAs; independent coupling yields a closed-form power allocation.
conclusion: Jointly accounting for measured radiation patterns and coupling efficiency is crucial for optimizing pinching-antenna systems.

title: Minkowski-Type Wasserstein Metrics And Barycenters For Location-Scale Mixtures With Application To Domain Adaptation
authors: Yunxin Zhang Songyan Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete optimal transport (OT) typically relies on pointwise matching between empirical measures, incurring computational costs that scale at least quadratically with the sample size. To circumvent this limitation, we introduce a mathematical framework for OT between finite location-scale mixture models. By defining a specific function class grounded in generalized Minkowski inequalities and characterizing OT maps between multivariate location-scale families, we extend Wasserstein-type metrics and barycenters to these mixture models under the assumption of identifiability. Furthermore, we prove that restricting joint couplings to a specific mixture structure reduces the continuous multimarginal OT problem to a discrete transport problem over mixture components. Computing transport plans between these components rather than individual samples reduces the computational complexity to linear scaling with respect to the sample size. Empirical evaluations on the VisDA-C benchmark confirm that this strategy achieves competitive accuracy compared to existing empirical OT approaches, while substantially reducing the computational cost and memory footprint.
tldr: This paper introduces Wasserstein-type metrics and barycenters for location-scale mixture models to reduce computational complexity in optimal transport.
motivation: Discrete optimal transport scales quadratically with sample size, limiting its application to large datasets.
method: The authors define a function class based on generalized Minkowski inequalities and characterize OT maps between multivariate location-scale families, reducing the continuous multimarginal OT problem to a discrete transport problem over mixture components.
result: The proposed method achieves linear scaling with sample size and competitive accuracy on the VisDA-C benchmark.
conclusion: This framework offers a computationally efficient alternative to empirical OT for domain adaptation and other applications.

title: Mean-Field PhiBE: Continuous-Time Mean-Field Reinforcement Learning From Discrete-Time Data
authors: Erhan Bayraktar, Martin Hernandez, Qinxin Yan, Yuhua Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses model-free continuous-time mean-field control in a setting where the population dynamics evolve continuously according to an unknown McKean-Vlasov stochastic differential equation, while only discrete-time transition data are available. In the model-based formulation, policy evaluation is naturally described by a stationary Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation on [MATH], but this equation involves the drift and diffusion coefficients of the controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics, which are not identifiable when only discrete-time data are available. On the other hand, a direct reduction to a time-discrete Bellman equation avoids the non-identifiability issue but loses the differential equation structure. To bridge these two viewpoints, we introduce a Mean-Field-PhiBE (MF-PhiBE), which incorporates discrete-time transition information into a continuous-time PDE on the Wasserstein space. The MF-PhiBE replaces the unknown infinitesimal drift and covariance in the policy-evaluation equation by one-step estimators computed from data, while preserving the generator structure of the McKean-Vlasov HJB equation. We also derive a policy-gradient theorem for entropy-regularized randomized feedback policies, expressing the actor direction through an action-wise infinitesimal advantage and the score of the policy. Combining these two ingredients yields a model-free actor-critic method. We prove a first-order consistency estimate showing that the value induced by an optimal MF-PhiBE policy approximates the optimal continuous-time value with an error of order [MATH]. In the linear-quadratic case, we show our approximation achieves second-order accuracy with only one-step data. Numerical experiments on an LQR benchmark and a crowd-aversion problem illustrate the proposed framework.
tldr: This paper develops a mean-field reinforcement learning method for continuous-time control using discrete-time data, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to solve model-free continuous-time mean-field control problems when only discrete-time transition data are available, addressing the non-identifiability of drift and diffusion coefficients.
method: They introduce a Mean-Field PhiBE (MF-PhiBE) that incorporates discrete-time transition information into a continuous-time PDE on Wasserstein space, and derive a policy-gradient theorem for entropy-regularized randomized feedback policies.
result: They prove first-order consistency and second-order accuracy in the linear-quadratic case, and demonstrate the framework on numerical experiments.
conclusion: The MF-PhiBE framework effectively bridges discrete-time data and continuous-time control in mean-field settings, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Maximizing Throughput In An M/g/1 Queue With Customer Abandonments
authors: Runhua Wu, Hayriye Ayhan, Douglas G. Down
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the problem of identifying the optimal server assignment policy in single-server queues with customer abandonment. We consider a system with Poisson arrivals and exponentially distributed patience times. We show that when service times follow either an Erlang-[MATH] or a hyperexponential distribution and the decision maker can observe the phase of a customer's service time, the Shortest Remaining Expected Processing Time (SREPT) policy maximizes the long-run average throughput, independent of the abandonment rate.

motivation: To identify the optimal policy for assigning servers to customers in a queue where customers may abandon, aiming to maximize long-run average throughput.
method: The authors analyze a single-server queue with Poisson arrivals, exponential patience, and Erlang or hyperexponential service times, proving that the Shortest Remaining Expected Processing Time (SREPT) policy is optimal.
result: The SREPT policy maximizes throughput independent of the abandonment rate for the considered service time distributions.
conclusion: The SREPT policy is optimal for throughput in this queueing model, providing a practical guideline for server assignment.

title: Three-Objective Integral R2 Subset Selection: NP-Hardness And Submodular Approximation
authors: Michael T. M. Emmerich
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Selecting a fixed number of representative points from a finite Pareto-front approximation is a fundamental post-processing task in multiobjective optimization. This paper studies this problem for the integral R2 indicator in three objectives, where the indicator is defined as the integral of the lower envelope of weighted Tchebycheff scalarizations over the two-dimensional weight simplex. We provide two complementary algorithmic results. On the positive side, we show that the integral R2 improvement with respect to any fixed baseline is a monotone submodular set function. For the usual ideal-point based R2 indicator, with the ideal point fixed, this yields a direct gap-reduction guarantee: greedy selection closes at least a [MATH]-fraction of the maximum possible R2 gap between a fixed dominated anchor value and the best cardinality-[MATH] value. We also give a tested greedy implementation that evaluates exact integral R2 values by subdivision, with worst-case running time [MATH]. On the negative side, we prove that exact fixed-cardinality subset selection is NP-hard already in three objectives. The hardness proof uses a perspective transformation that maps Tchebycheff-shadow improvements to a weighted anchored-box union problem with density [MATH], and then adapts the three-dimensional anchored-box construction of Bringmann, Cabello, and Emmerich. Together, these results separate the tractable two-objective case from the three-objective case while identifying a principled approximation route based on submodular optimization.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity and approximation of subset selection for the integral R2 indicator in three-objective optimization.
motivation: Selecting representative points from a Pareto-front approximation is a key post-processing task in multiobjective optimization, and the integral R2 indicator is a quality measure that requires efficient selection algorithms.

title: Scalable Operator Learning Via Nystr\"om Approximation With Denoising Applications
authors: Naveen Gupta, Vaibhav Silmana, S. Sivananthan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study Nystr\"om subsampling for vector-valued regression in vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. Standard kernel methods often suffer from prohibitive computational costs due to the construction and inversion of large kernel matrices, which limits their scalability to large datasets. To overcome this bottleneck, we propose an efficient operator learning algorithm based on Nystr\"om subsampling that accommodates functional outputs. Under general source conditions characterized by index functions-extending beyond the classical H\"older-type and operator-monotone frameworks-we establish minimax-optimal convergence rates for the proposed estimator. As an application of the proposed framework, we consider function denoising problems. Unlike classical denoising methods, which are typically tailored to specific signal representations or noise models, our approach formulates denoising within a general operator learning framework. Numerical experiments on signal denoising, real-time audio denoising, image denoising, inverse Radon transform reconstruction, and energy-efficiency prediction confirm that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to full kernel methods while substantially reducing computational cost.
tldr: This paper proposes a scalable operator learning method using Nyström approximation for vector-valued regression, with applications in denoising.
motivation: Standard kernel methods are computationally expensive for large datasets due to large kernel matrices. The authors aim to develop an efficient algorithm that scales to large datasets while maintaining accuracy.
method: The method uses Nyström subsampling to approximate the kernel matrix in vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, and establishes minimax-optimal convergence rates under general source conditions.
result: The proposed algorithm achieves performance comparable to full kernel methods on various denoising tasks (signal, audio, image, inverse Radon transform) while substantially reducing computational cost.
conclusion: Nyström subsampling is an effective approach for scalable operator learning, enabling efficient denoising without sacrificing accuracy.

title: A Geometric Approach To Inner Problems Associated With Exponentially Small Splitting Phenomena In Local Bifurcations
authors: Kristian Uldall Kristiansen

title: Tvd And Tvb Preservation Without Tvd Time Discretization For Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
authors: Zheng Sun Ziyao Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Total variation diminishing (TVD) and total variation bounded (TVB) properties are crucial for controlling spurious oscillations in numerical solutions of conservation laws. In the classical Runge--Kutta (RK) discontinuous Galerkin (DG) framework, enforcing these properties is intrinsically tied to TVD time integrators, more commonly known today as strong-stability-preserving (SSP) methods. This reliance imposes severe structural restrictions, including order barriers and incompatibility with various fully discrete DG formulations, ranging from the recent RKDG method with compact stencils (cRKDG) to the widely established Arbitrary DERivative (ADER) DG method. To bypass these constraints, we propose a novel trace-limited corrector framework that preserves the TVD/TVB-in-the-means properties using generic, non-SSP time stepping. Based on Harten's lemma, our key insight is that total variation stability is dictated solely by the cell-average update in the final corrector stage. Consequently, we modify the traces in the numerical fluxes exclusively in the final stage, leaving the intermediate predictor stages unconstrained. This strategy decouples oscillation control from the SSP restriction, accommodates standard RKDG, cRKDG, and ADER-DG predictors, and retains the compactness of the cRKDG framework. We also prove that the limiter does not activate in smooth regions, thereby preserving the underlying accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the capabilities and robustness of the method.
tldr: This paper proposes a trace-limited corrector framework for discontinuous Galerkin methods that preserves TVD/TVB properties without requiring SSP time integrators.
motivation: Classical TVD/TVB enforcement in RKDG methods relies on SSP time stepping, which imposes order barriers and incompatibility with certain DG formulations like cRKDG and ADER-DG.
method: The authors modify the traces in numerical fluxes only in the final corrector stage, based on Harten's lemma, to decouple oscillation control from SSP restrictions.
result: The framework works with generic non-SSP time stepping, retains compactness, and does not activate the limiter in smooth regions, preserving accuracy.
conclusion: The proposed method enables TVD/TVB preservation in a broader class of DG methods without the constraints of SSP integrators.

title: Regularization Of The Metric Generalized Inverse In Banach Spaces And The Dichotomy Phenomenon
authors: Bernd Hofmann Peter Math\'e
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a bounded linear operator acting between Banach spaces, its metric generalized inverse is the analog to the prominent Moore-Penrose inverse for operators acting between Hilbert spaces. This generalized inverse is well-defined for Banach spaces that are strictly convex and reflexive. Previous studies had been restricted to closed range situations, where the metric generalized inverse constitutes a continuous homogeneous mapping. The focus of the present study is on the ill-posed situation in the sense of Nashed, when the governing operator has a non-closed range. We define and analyze iterative schemes as the Landweber and the Schulz-Newton method, as well as parametric schemes with focus on a specific Tikhonov method. Both types are called regularizations aimed at approximating the metric generalized inverse. As a fundamental feature of such schemes we observe a dichotomy. This emphasizes that these schemes, when applied to elements of the domain of the metric generalized inverse, approximate the corresponding best approximate solutions well, whereas the resulting approximations will be asymptotically unbounded if they are applied to elements that do not belong to the domain of the metric generalized inverse.
tldr: This paper studies regularization methods for the metric generalized inverse of bounded linear operators in Banach spaces, focusing on the ill-posed case with non-closed range.
motivation: To extend the theory of metric generalized inverses from closed-range to non-closed-range operators, which is important for solving ill-posed inverse problems in Banach spaces.
method: The authors analyze iterative schemes (Landweber, Schulz-Newton) and parametric schemes (Tikhonov regularization) to approximate the metric generalized inverse, and prove a dichotomy property.
result: The schemes converge for elements in the domain of the metric generalized inverse, but yield asymptotically unbounded approximations for elements outside the domain.
conclusion: The dichotomy phenomenon is a fundamental feature of these regularization schemes, highlighting the need for careful application in ill-posed problems.

title: Dimension Spectrum Of Continued Fraction Expansions With Coefficients Restricted To The Fibonacci Sequence
authors: Amit Priyadarshi Arpit Dawar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we analyze the structure of the dimension spectrum of continued fraction expansions with coefficients restricted to the generalized Fibonacci sequence. Let [MATH] denote the generalized Fibonacci sequence starting with the positive integers [MATH]. We prove that the continued fractions whose digits lie in [MATH] have full dimension spectrum for every [MATH] such that [MATH], or [MATH] and [MATH]. On the other hand, using the numerical tools developed by Falk and Nussbaum, we show that the dimension spectrum has a gap for continued fractions with digits restricted to each of the sets [MATH] and [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the set of Lucas numbers. Moreover, for [MATH] and [MATH], we prove that the dimension spectrum always contains a non-trivial interval.
tldr: This paper studies the dimension spectrum of continued fraction expansions with digits restricted to generalized Fibonacci sequences.
motivation: To understand the fractal structure of continued fractions with restricted digit sets, specifically those arising from Fibonacci-like sequences.
method: The authors use analytical techniques and numerical tools developed by Falk and Nussbaum to compute and analyze the dimension spectrum.
result: They prove that for certain parameter ranges the dimension spectrum is full, while for others (e.g., Lucas numbers) it has a gap.
conclusion: The dimension spectrum of such continued fractions can be either full or contain gaps depending on the digit set, revealing nontrivial structure.

title: Artin Monoids, Their Homomorphisms And Twins
authors: Arkady Berenstein, Jacob Greenstein, Jian-Rong Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the twin homomorphism problem for Coxeter groups and the corresponding Hecke monoids, we find a large class of its solutions originating from standard homomorphisms of Artin monoids and their compositions. These homomorphisms are expected to be injective when they are optimal and injective on generators, which generalizes the homogeneous homomorphisms and the famous Tits conjecture recently settled by Paris. We classify disjoint standard homomorphisms and conjecture the complete classification when the domain is of rank two.
tldr: This paper studies Artin monoids, their homomorphisms, and the twin problem, which is purely algebraic and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The authors aim to solve the twin homomorphism problem for Coxeter groups and Hecke monoids by studying standard homomorphisms of Artin monoids.
method: They classify disjoint standard homomorphisms and conjecture complete classification for rank-two domains, using algebraic techniques.
result: They find a large class of solutions to the twin problem originating from standard homomorphisms and their compositions.
conclusion: The work generalizes homogeneous homomorphisms and the Tits conjecture, but remains within pure mathematics.

title: Recycling Singular And Projection Subspaces For Pseudospectra Computation
authors: Kuan Xu Kuan Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing matrix pseudospectra over a prescribed region requires evaluating the smallest singular value of [MATH] at a large number of grid points, which can be prohibitively expensive for large-scale matrices. We develop a recycling-based framework for accelerating such computations for both dense and sparse matrices. The main idea is to exploit the correlation between singular value problems at neighboring grid points by adaptively recycling singular subspaces computed at previously visited points by an iterative SVD solver. We develop fast Rayleigh-Ritz-SVD procedures for extracting Ritz singular pairs from the recycled singular subspaces, together with fast residual evaluation procedures, with an overall cost that scales linearly with the number of recycled samples. When the iterative SVD solver admits preconditioning, we propose using a two-level preconditioner whose projection subspaces are recycled. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed recycling strategies yield substantial speedups over existing methods while maintaining the accuracy of the computed pseudospectra.
tldr: This paper develops a recycling-based framework to accelerate pseudospectra computation for large-scale matrices.
motivation: Computing matrix pseudospectra over a region requires evaluating the smallest singular value at many grid points, which is expensive for large matrices.
method: The method exploits correlation between singular value problems at neighboring grid points by recycling singular subspaces from previously visited points, using fast Rayleigh-Ritz-SVD procedures and residual evaluation.
result: Numerical experiments show substantial speedups over existing methods while maintaining accuracy.
conclusion: Recycling singular subspaces is an effective strategy for accelerating pseudospectra computation.

title: Second-order Methods For Multiobjective Composite Optimization: Preconditioning Strategies, Subspace Variants And Inexact Solutions
authors: Xinmin Yang Jian Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiobjective composite optimization problems arise in sparse regularization, constrained multiobjective models, and multi-task learning, but their numerical solution remains challenging when the smooth components are ill-conditioned. Proximal gradient methods are inexpensive per iteration but may converge slowly, while proximal Newton and quasi-Newton methods exploit curvature information at the cost of evaluating expensive metric proximal mappings. To address these issues, we propose a preconditioned proximal Barzilai--Borwein method for multiobjective composite optimization. The method combines objective-wise Barzilai--Borwein scaling, which reduces imbalance among objectives, with a common preconditioner that captures shared curvature information. To avoid non-diagonal metric proximal mappings, we develop a subspace variant in which the search direction is computed in a two-dimensional subspace generated by a proximal-gradient-type direction and a projected historical direction. By constructing a conjugate basis with respect to the preconditioning metric, the subspace model decomposes into tractable one-dimensional subproblems. The framework is further extended to nonsmooth terms of the form [MATH] through a linear-operator-aware preconditioner, yielding explicit proximal evaluations via dual subproblems. We also analyze an inexact version based on relaxed descent conditions. We establish the global convergence of the inexact algorithm in the nonconvex setting and prove a linear convergence rate under an error-bound condition. Numerical experiments on ill-conditioned [MATH]-regularized, structured [MATH]-regularized, and linearly constrained problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper proposes preconditioned proximal gradient and Newton-type methods for multiobjective composite optimization, focusing on numerical optimization techniques.
motivation: Multiobjective composite optimization problems are challenging when smooth components are ill-conditioned; existing methods are either slow or require expensive metric proximal mappings.
method: The authors develop a preconditioned proximal Barzilai-Borwein method with objective-wise scaling and a common preconditioner, a subspace variant using a two-dimensional search direction, and an inexact version with relaxed descent conditions.
result: Global convergence is established for the inexact algorithm in the nonconvex setting, and linear convergence is proved under an error-bound condition. Numerical experiments on ill-conditioned problems demonstrate effectiveness.
conclusion: The proposed methods improve efficiency for multiobjective composite optimization, particularly for ill-conditioned problems, by combining preconditioning and subspace techniques.

title: The Educational Proof Assistant Waterproof In An Introductory Proof Course: Proof Construction And Learning Processes
authors: Pim Otte, Rogier Bos, Johan Commelin, Jim Portegies
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the use of an educational proof assistant in an introductory proof course through a quasi-experiment in a varied setting: multiple teachers, students with different study programs, and a mixed Dutch-English language environment. First-year university students are known to struggle with writing proofs. Waterproof is a proof assistant that is designed to support the transfer of skills to paper proofs by working with controlled natural language. We focus on the students' ability to construct valid mathematical proofs, and on their learning process. We study this through in-class observation, surveys, and analysis of student performance and proof structure. We present evidence that effects of using an educational proof assistant carry over to the pen-and-paper context,even when the assistant is English and the proof is given in Dutch. We also present evidence that suggests students in the Mathematics-Computer Science program achieve higher grades when using Waterproof. Our most important conclusion is that an educational proof assistant can help students be more explicit in their proofs. As students self-selected into using Waterproof rather than being randomly assigned, these results are suggestive rather than causal.
tldr: This paper studies the use of an educational proof assistant in an introductory proof course, focusing on proof construction and learning processes.
motivation: First-year university students struggle with writing proofs; the authors investigate whether an educational proof assistant can help transfer skills to pen-and-paper proofs.
method: A quasi-experiment with multiple teachers, students from different programs, and a mixed Dutch-English environment; data from in-class observation, surveys, and analysis of student performance and proof structure.
result: Evidence suggests that using the proof assistant carries over to pen-and-paper context and may improve grades for Mathematics-Computer Science students; students become more explicit in their proofs.
conclusion: Educational proof assistants can help students be more explicit in proofs, but results are suggestive rather than causal due to self-selection.

title: Numerical Analysis Of First-order Mean Field Games Under Displacement Monotonicity
authors: Yohance A. P. Osborne Alp\'ar R. M\'esz\'aros
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a particle method for the numerical approximation of time-dependent first-order Mean Field Games (MFGs) systems with non-separable, displacement monotone Hamiltonians and terminal costs, for arbitrary time-horizons and (possibly) singular initial player distributions in [MATH]. The numerical scheme is based on an implicit Euler discretization in time and sampling in space of the characteristic Hamiltonian/Pontryagin system associated with the continuous MFGs system. We prove convergence of the approximations of the player distribution in the [MATH]-metric and the approximations for the gradient of the value function along optimal trajectories in the [MATH]-norm as the number of spatial samples tends to infinity jointly with the temporal time-step vanishing. The error bound that we establish for this convergence further implies rates of convergence of the scheme for a range of spatial sampling techniques. Provided that the Lagrangian and terminal costs are additionally locally Lipschitz continuous, we also establish an asymptotic error bound in the [MATH]-norm for the approximations of the value function along optimal trajectories. This is the first work in the literature on rigorous numerical approximation and analysis of first-order MFG systems that handles non-separable Hamiltonians and potentially singular initial agent distributions for arbitrary long time horizons. We illustrate the performance of the scheme in numerical experiments for a range of initial agent distributions, time horizons and space dimensions.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for approximating first-order Mean Field Games with displacement monotone Hamiltonians, focusing on convergence analysis and error bounds.
motivation: Mean Field Games model large populations of interacting agents, but numerical methods for non-separable Hamiltonians and singular initial distributions are lacking.
method: The authors propose a particle method using implicit Euler time discretization and spatial sampling of the characteristic Hamiltonian/Pontryagin system, proving convergence in the 1-Wasserstein metric and L2 norm.
result: Convergence rates are established for the player distribution and gradient of the value function, with numerical experiments illustrating performance across various settings.
conclusion: This is the first rigorous numerical analysis for first-order MFGs with non-separable Hamiltonians, handling arbitrary time horizons and singular initial distributions.

title: On Lefschetz's Point-free Periodicity
authors: Alejandro O. Majadas-Moure
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We motivate two new approaches to the study of Lefschetz point-free periodicity. The first focusses on spaces satisfying the Wecken property. As an example, we study the bubble spaces. The second is a relative study of the Lefschetz point-free periodicity. This becomes important, for example, in the study of repellers of dynamical systems.
tldr: The paper introduces new approaches to Lefschetz point-free periodicity in topology, focusing on Wecken property and relative periodicity.
motivation: To develop novel frameworks for studying point-free periodicity in dynamical systems and topological spaces.
method: Two approaches: one using spaces with the Wecken property (e.g., bubble spaces), and a relative study of Lefschetz point-free periodicity.
result: New theoretical insights into point-free periodicity, with applications to repellers in dynamical systems.
conclusion: The proposed approaches provide new tools for analyzing periodic behavior in topological dynamics.

title: Separation, Constraint Qualifications, And Cycling In Outer Approximation
authors: Jan Kronqvist Erik Tamm
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The outer approximation algorithm is a widely used method for solving convex mixed-integer nonlinear programs. While the algorithm is well established in theory and practice, certain assumptions underlying its convergence are rarely discussed in the literature. In this paper, we examine two such assumptions: that a constraint qualification holds at the optimal solution of each nonlinear programming subproblem, and that these subproblems can be solved exactly. We argue that both assumptions are connected to the issue of cycling, by which we mean that the same integer assignment reappears in successive iterations of the algorithm. When a constraint qualification fails, separation of the current iterate from the feasible set is not guaranteed, which can cause the algorithm to stall. When the nonlinear programming subproblem is solved only approximately, separation may likewise fail, and we show that high precision can be required in certain cases. To formalize the connection between these issues, we prove that when Slater's condition is nearly violated, a point close to the exact solution can be found at which separation fails. Furthermore, within the outer approximation algorithm, we propose to use extended cutting planes as a fallback strategy when cycling is detected. We prove that this approach yields a finitely convergent algorithm under relaxed assumptions regarding constraint qualifications, thereby generalizing the convergence theory of the outer approximation algorithm.
tldr: This paper analyzes constraint qualifications and cycling in the outer approximation algorithm for convex mixed-integer nonlinear programming.
motivation: The outer approximation algorithm is widely used but its convergence relies on assumptions like constraint qualifications and exact subproblem solutions, which are rarely examined.
method: The authors prove that when Slater's condition is nearly violated, separation can fail, and propose extended cutting planes as a fallback to handle cycling.
result: They show that the extended cutting plane approach yields a finitely convergent algorithm under relaxed assumptions about constraint qualifications.
conclusion: The work generalizes the convergence theory of the outer approximation algorithm by addressing practical issues like cycling and constraint qualification failures.

title: Multiscale Exit-Join Dynamics: Tactical Consensus And Strategic Coalition Formation
authors: Quanyan Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a multiscale model of coalition formation in which strategic exit-and-join decisions are coupled with tactical consensus dynamics inside coalitions. Coalition value is generated endogenously from within-coalition information aggregation, while Aumann-Dreze payoffs, switching frictions, and acceptance rules govern strategic reconfiguration. The framework introduces a fast-slow architecture in which transferable coalition value emerges from DeGroot-style consensus processes, while coalition structures evolve through incentive-driven exit-and-join dynamics. The analysis characterizes joint tactical-strategic equilibria, conditions for tactical and strategic unanimity, segregation, polarization, and cognitive barriers that sustain stable coalition structures. A fixed-point characterization and existence results are established for the coupled dynamics. Numerical experiments reveal an instability-consensus paradox: low or negative switching barriers may prevent strategic convergence while simultaneously promoting temporal mixing sufficient to achieve global tactical consensus. The results provide a unified perspective on coalition formation, consensus dynamics, information aggregation, and strategic stability in multi-agent systems.
tldr: This paper develops a multiscale model of coalition formation combining strategic exit-join decisions with tactical consensus dynamics, using a fast-slow architecture and DeGroot-style consensus.
motivation: To understand how coalition structures evolve endogenously from within-coalition information aggregation and strategic reconfiguration, and to characterize joint tactical-strategic equilibria.
method: The framework couples fast consensus dynamics (DeGroot model) with slow coalition structure evolution via exit-join decisions, Aumann-Dreze payoffs, switching frictions, and acceptance rules. Fixed-point characterization and existence results are established.
result: Numerical experiments reveal an instability-consensus paradox: low or negative switching barriers may prevent strategic convergence while enabling global tactical consensus.
conclusion: The model provides a unified perspective on coalition formation, consensus dynamics, and strategic stability in multi-agent systems.

title: Mirage: Protecting Against Malicious Image Editing Via False Moderation
authors: Anshul Nasery, Ramnath Kumar, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Sewoong Oh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The proliferation of AI-powered image editing systems raises serious concerns because it allows personal images to be arbitrarily manipulated at scale, with minimal effort, and a lower barrier to entry. Prior work on image immunization adds imperceptible perturbations to an image to protect against unauthorized manipulations. However, these methods usually require access to the model weights and the image manipulating prompt. This significantly limits their use, especially against powerful commercial image-editors such as GPT-Image, Gemini Flash Image (Nano Banana), and Grok Imagine. To address this, we take a system-level view of the problem and identify a previously unexplored attack surface common to all major commercial image editing systems: pre-generation safety moderation.Rather than disrupting the generative model itself, we propose to immunize images by causing these moderation classifiers to flag images as policy-violating, triggering an automatic refusal regardless of the editing prompt. We operationalize this by adding adversarial perturbations to align our image to policy-violating concepts in the representation space of an ensemble of open-source embedding and moderation models. We call our method MIRAGE, which stands for Moderation Induced Resistance Against Generative Editing. We evaluate MIRAGE against multiple closed-source image editing APIs and demonstrate success rates of more than 88%. Our approach is simple, prompt-agnostic, and effective, offering a practical path towards protecting personal images from unauthorized AI-powered editing.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to protect images from unauthorized AI editing by triggering safety moderation classifiers to refuse editing, rather than disrupting the generative model itself.
motivation: Existing image immunization methods require access to model weights and prompts, limiting their use against commercial image editors. The authors aim to provide a practical, prompt-agnostic defense.
method: MIRAGE adds adversarial perturbations to images so that they are misclassified as policy-violating by an ensemble of open-source embedding and moderation models, causing automatic refusal by the editing system.
result: The method achieves over 88% success rate against multiple closed-source image editing APIs, including GPT-Image and Gemini Flash Image.
conclusion: MIRAGE offers a simple, effective, and practical path to protect personal images from unauthorized AI-powered editing by exploiting pre-generation safety moderation.

title: Data Facts: A Metadata Schema For Structured Data Exchange In The NANDini Multi-Agent Ecosystem
authors: Jin Gao, Maria Gorskikh, Pradyumna Chari, Brittany Box, Mukul Kemla, Pratik Behera, Abhishek Mehta, Ramesh Raskar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: NANDini (Networked Agents Natural Distillation of Interconnected Nodal Intelligence) envisions an automated ecosystem where intelligent agents independently create, process, and exchange data to drive decisions at scale. Realizing this vision requires infrastructure beyond agent discovery and communication: agents must be able to advertise, evaluate, and verify the datasets they hold. Current protocols, including NANDA for federated registry and A2A and MCP for inter-agent messaging, address identity and communication but provide no mechanism for structured data exchange. Existing enterprise data-sharing frameworks, such as IDS-RAM, Gaia-X, and Ocean Protocol, assume human-in-the-loop governance that is incompatible with autonomous, real-time agent interactions. We introduce Data Facts, a core NANDini concept: a lightweight JSON metadata schema that bridges agent discovery and data access through a single pointer, `data_facts_url`, added to an existing Agent Facts registry record.
